forecasters.name: Dixon-Coles (Bayesian-shrunk)
forecasters.headline: England are a clear favourite to beat DR Congo (67.1% to win).

drivers.label: Attack vs defence
drivers.detail: England's attack is projected for about 1.9 goals against DR Congo's defence, versus roughly 0.6 the other way — the scoring gap is what tilts the call.

drivers.label: Goal-creation strength
drivers.detail: England carries the stronger end-to-end goal output in their FIFA match stats, so they convert more of their chances into the projected scoreline.

drivers.label: Low-scoring caution
drivers.detail: Both sides project to score few goals, and tight games like this end level more often than raw averages suggest — that keeps the draw alive at 23.3%.

forecasters.methodNote: Market-blind: each team's FIFA on-pitch scoring rate (xG-for and goals-against, Bayesian-shrunk toward an Elo strength prior in the profile layer) is mapped to relative attack/defence strengths, combined via the Maher multiplicative model into per-team goal expectations on a neutral venue, then expanded into a Dixon-Coles score matrix with low-score dependence rho=-0.1 (league baseline 1.5 goals/side, goal scale 1); cell probabilities are collapsed to win/draw/win. No betting odds or prediction-market prices were used at any step.

forecasters.name: xG-corrected Elo
forecasters.headline: England are the clear favourite to beat DR Congo, winning roughly 73 times out of 100 to DR Congo's 9.

drivers.label: Chance-creation form
drivers.detail: Across the group stage England created 1.6 more good chances per game than they gave up, versus 0.3 for DR Congo — England simply made better chances more often.

drivers.label: Earned standing, not lucky results
drivers.detail: England are rated on how convincingly they out-created opponents, not on tight scorelines, so wins built on real dominance count more than results that hinged on a single lucky goal.

drivers.label: Margin of safety
drivers.detail: The gap is wide enough that DR Congo would need a clear upset to advance.

forecasters.methodNote: Market-blind: each team's pre-tournament Elo prior is replayed through the group stage using expected-goal difference as the match outcome — a logistic merit score S_xG = 1/(1+e^(-1.8·xGD)) drives a standard Elo update (scale 400, K=24) so chance-creation, not the raw scoreline, moves ratings; the fixture is then converted to 1X2 via a Davidson ties model on the neutral-venue rating difference. Inputs are FIFA on-pitch xG and Elo priors only — no betting or prediction-market data was used.

forecasters.name: PRODEGY split attack/defence Elo
forecasters.headline: England is clearly favoured, expected to generate the better scoring chances over 90 minutes.

drivers.label: Attack vs defence
drivers.detail: England has been creating about 2.3 goals of chances a game; DR Congo's defence usually allows about 1.2. That points to roughly 2.4 goals for England.

drivers.label: Defence vs attack
drivers.detail: DR Congo has been creating about 1.1 goals of chances a game; England's defence usually allows about 0.7. That points to roughly 1.8 goals for DR Congo.

drivers.label: Two-way balance
drivers.detail: Across both ends, England projects to outscore DR Congo by about 0.7 goals on the night.

forecasters.methodNote: Market-blind: independent offence (xOS) and defence (xDS) ratings in goal units, seeded from pre-tournament Elo priors and updated sequentially over group-stage FIFA xG (rate 0.15) against each opponent's opposing rating. Fixture goal rates lambda = xOS_A - xDS_B + base and mu = xOS_B - xDS_A + base feed an independent-Poisson score matrix; 1X2 read off and normalised. No betting or prediction-market data was used.

forecasters.name: Physical-decay dynamic-K Elo
forecasters.headline: England is clearly the stronger side here with about a 72% chance to win, partly because the other side ran a heavier physical load and is likelier to tire.

drivers.label: Physical load
drivers.detail: England ran a heavier high-intensity workload in the group stage than DR Congo, leaving it more likely to tire and fade as this match wears on.

drivers.label: Form and strength
drivers.detail: England carried stronger group-stage results into this fixture and starts as the on-paper favourite.

drivers.label: Rest edge
drivers.detail: DR Congo comes in with the better turnaround between matches and should be the fresher side at kickoff.

forecasters.methodNote: Market-blind: dynamic-K Elo replayed over group-stage results, seeded from pre-tournament Elo priors. Each rating update used a learning rate scaled by the team's relative sprint load (sprints + high-speed runs per minute) and a knockout stage weight. At prediction time each team's effective rating is reduced by a fatigue penalty proportional to how far its average high-intensity running distance exceeded the field mean, and the rating gap is mapped to a 1X2 distribution via a Davidson-tie logistic (scale 400, no home advantage, draw nu 0.7). No betting or prediction-market data was used.

forecasters.name: Tactical style-clash mElo
forecasters.headline: England is the slight favourite — its game style matches up well against DR Congo.

drivers.label: Overall quality
drivers.detail: England has been the stronger side across the group stage, scoring more freely and conceding less.

drivers.label: Style matchup
drivers.detail: England leans on keeping the ball while DR Congo leans on sitting in a deep block; that clash tilts the game toward England.

drivers.label: How even it is
drivers.detail: England controls the kind of game it wants to play, which is why we make it the pick rather than a coin flip.

forecasters.methodNote: Market-blind: multidimensional Elo (mElo). Each team carries a learned scalar rating mu (logistic gradient ascent on group-stage results, draws as 0.5, priors seeded from centred Elo) plus a fixed 4D tactical embedding c built from FIFA possession / high-press / counter-attack / low-block z-scores. Head-to-head advantage A = (mu_A - mu_B) + 0.35 * c_A^T Omega c_B with Omega block-diagonal cyclic [[0,1],[-1,0]], giving an antisymmetric non-transitive style-clash term; win prob = sigmoid(A), draw split via Davidson nu=0.85. Uses only on-pitch FIFA statistics and pre-tournament Elo priors — no market data was used.

forecasters.name: Line-breaks & offers efficiency (gradient-boosted)
forecasters.headline: England are clear favourites to beat DR Congo, mostly on cleaner attacking play.

drivers.label: Breaking through the defence
drivers.detail: England completed line-breaking passes more reliably, slicing through DR Congo's lines more often.

drivers.label: Converting chances
drivers.detail: England turned more of its forward runs into real scoring looks than DR Congo did.

drivers.label: Scoring vs leaking goals
drivers.detail: England created more and conceded less across the group stage, a stronger net goal balance.

drivers.label: Controlling the ball
drivers.detail: England held possession noticeably more, keeping DR Congo chasing the game.

forecasters.methodNote: Market-blind: per-team penetration/creation profiles (line-break success, 4-unit penetration share, offer conversion, shrunk attack/defence rates, possession) are differenced (team A − team B) into one feature vector. Three one-vs-rest gradient-boosted regression ensembles (40 rounds, depth 3, learning rate 0.1), trained on leakage-safe group-stage rows (each match seen only with prior-match profiles), score the home/draw/away outcomes; scores are clamped to [0,1] and normalised to sum to 1. No betting odds, prices, or market-implied probabilities were used.

forecasters.name: Passing-network structure (random forest)
forecasters.headline: England is the clear favourite (71%) — its passing play is the harder one to break down.

drivers.label: Passing structure
drivers.detail: England spreads passes across more players and fewer go through one pivot, so it keeps more routes forward when pressed. (Passing-network detail was unavailable, so this leans on possession and pressing instead.)

drivers.label: Ball control
drivers.detail: England keeps the ball more (55% vs 44%), dictating the tempo of build-up.

drivers.label: Scoring threat
drivers.detail: England has created the better chances on average (2.07 vs 1.09 expected goals a game).

forecasters.methodNote: Market-blind: three one-vs-rest random forests (60 CART trees each, depth 5, 70% feature subsampling) over the A-minus-B difference of passing-network graph features (density, centralization, top-5 edge share) and style features (possession, high-press share, expected-goal rate); forest scores are clamped to [0,1] and normalised to a 1X2 distribution. Training rows are leakage-safe (each rebuilt from matches strictly before its date) and fall back to a logistic model on structure and attack gaps under eight rows. No betting or market data was used.

forecasters.name: Stacked Ensemble
forecasters.headline: Pulling every angle together, England is narrowly the side to back here, at about a 49% chance to win.

drivers.label: Model agreement
drivers.detail: 100% of the underlying views lean England, so the blended call sides with England with confidence.

drivers.label: How settled
drivers.detail: No single outcome dominates — England edges it, but the result is close to a toss-up.

forecasters.methodNote: Market-blind: ridge-logistic stack over the 7 base models. Each base view contributes its P(England win) and P(draw) as features; three one-vs-rest logistic heads (L2=1) trained on 72 prior matches produce class scores that are clamped and renormalised to a 1X2 triple. Falls back to an equal-weight logarithmic opinion pool of the base views when the sample is thin or an outcome is unseen. No betting odds or market-implied probabilities were used at any stage.

forecasters.name: Multi-calibrated 8-in-1
forecasters.headline: Blending all 8 models and correcting for known group-stage biases, England is the call here at about 62%.

drivers.label: Consensus of all models
drivers.detail: The eight model views are pooled into one balanced consensus before any adjustment, which favours England at 62%.

drivers.label: Bias correction
drivers.detail: The consensus is nudged to fix biases the models showed on group matches of this type, shifting England's win chance by 0 points.

forecasters.methodNote: Market-blind: equal-weight linear (arithmetic) opinion pool of all 8 model views (seven base models + the stacked ensemble), then MCBoost multicalibration (alpha=0.15, 5 correction round(s)) learned on the group stage across overlapping style/strength subgroups, replayed on this fixture and bounded to within 12pp per outcome of the consensus. No betting or market-implied probabilities were used at any stage.
